lines.trans: Elena, are you hiring cooks through an ad?
Hello, Viktor Petrovich. Yes, we are expanding.
You had better put a sign near the metro!
There is no need for that.
Normal professionals do not look for work in newspapers.
Excellent candidates have already come to me.
And from which restaurants are these people?
Some work in very respectable places.
Could someone really be leaving good restaurants?
Maybe even from your restaurant.
I will eat my chef's hat if my cooks leave!
Then in advance I wish you bon appétit!
My people are loyal to me to the end.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
I'm listening right by my ear.
The car is parked near the house.

examples.text: Возле дома Аникеева ходили два подозрительных человека.
examples.trans: Near Anikeev's house two suspicious people were walking.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'newspaper' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нормальные профессионалы не ищут работу по газетам.
examples.trans: Normal professionals do not look for work in newspapers.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
достойная старость = a comfortable, dignified old age

examples.text: А мы обеспечим вам достойную старость.
examples.trans: And we will ensure you a comfortable old age.

examples.text: Отдайте это видео мне. А мы обеспечим вам достойную старость.
examples.trans: Give this video to me. And we will ensure you a comfortable old age.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
+ dative of person + genitive of thing: желаю вам удачи

examples.trans: Good health to you, sir! (I wish you health!)

meanings.en: in advance, beforehand, ahead of time

examples.trans: Did you set all this up in advance?

examples.text: Мы купили билеты на поезд заранее.
examples.trans: We bought the train tickets in advance.

examples.text: Тогда заранее желаю вам приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Then in advance I wish you bon appétit!

meanings.note: polite, or to several people; the first в is silent

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look for'.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: in an election or for a job

examples.trans: He is a candidate for mayor.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'chef's hat' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The chef wears a white chef's hat.

examples.text: Я съем колпак, если мои повара уйдут!
examples.trans: I will eat my chef's hat if my cooks leave!
I will eat my chef's hat!

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'someone, somebody' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.
The metro station is located nearby.
You had better put a sign near the metro!

examples.text: Тогда встречаемся в семь часов около метро.
examples.trans: Then we meet at seven o'clock near the metro.
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

набирать.gloss: to gain, gather, recruit; to dial

meanings.en: to dial (a phone number); to recruit

examples.trans: The firm is recruiting new employees.

examples.text: Он теперь набирает популярность. И Осипенко может проиграть выборы.
examples.trans: He is now gaining popularity. And Osipenko might lose the election.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a chance.

examples.text: Некоторым сама жизнь даёт второй шанс.
examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a second chance.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'обходимость'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'necessity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is no need for that.
There is no need for that.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.text: Неужели так трудно найти хороший сюжет?
examples.trans: Is it really so difficult to find a good story?

examples.text: Неужели президент накажет вас за правду?
examples.trans: Will the president really punish you for the truth?
Do you really not care at all?
I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.
I found the job through an ad.
A notice is hanging on the door.

examples.text: По объявлению. Девочка — сирота, у неё трагедия.
examples.trans: Through an ad. The girl is an orphan, she has a tragedy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.
I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.
Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'анный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('devoted, loyal').

examples.trans: My friends are loyal to me.

examples.text: Мои люди преданы мне до конца.
examples.trans: My people are loyal to me to the end.
I am devoted to the chef.
Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.
Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'фессионал'). Common masculine noun meaning 'professional' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас тут в провинции одни профессионалы.
examples.trans: You've got nothing but professionals out here in the provinces.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'ширяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to expand'.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, Виктор Петрович. Да, мы расширяемся.
examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich. Yes, we are expanding.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'sign, plaque' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A sign hangs near the entrance.
You had better put a sign near the metro!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to leave, to go away, to walk out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away (on foot)', paired with 'уходить'.

meanings.en: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
